title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Release of the 19th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en:
1. The application of 'other illegal business operations that seriously disrupt market order' as provided in Item (4) of Article 225 of the Criminal Law shall be determined based on whether the relevant conduct has social harmfulness, criminal illegality, and necessity of criminal punishment equivalent to the illegal business operations specified in Items (1) to (3) of Article 225 of the Criminal Law.

2. In determining whether a business operation that violates administrative regulations constitutes the crime of illegal business operations, consideration shall be given to whether such business operation seriously disrupts market order. A business operation that, although violating administrative regulations, has not yet seriously disrupted market order, shall not be deemed to constitute the crime of illegal business operations.
keywords_en: criminal; crime of illegal business operations; seriously disrupting market order; social harmfulness; criminal illegality; necessity of criminal punishment
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Release of the 19th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2018] No. 338

To the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon deliberation and decision by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the following five cases (Guiding Cases No. 97-101), including the case of Wang Lijun for illegal business operation that was retried and acquitted, are hereby released as the 19th Batch of Guiding Cases for reference in the adjudication of similar cases.

December 19, 2018

Guiding Case No. 97

Wang Lijun v. — retrial for acquittal on charge of illegal business operation

(Released by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 19, 2018)

Keywords: Criminal; illegal business operation; severely disrupting market order; social harmfulness; criminal illegality; necessity of criminal punishment

Ruling Gist:

1. The application of the provision on "other illegal business operations that severely disrupt market order" under Item (4) of Article 225 of the Criminal Law shall be determined based on whether the relevant conduct possesses social harmfulness, criminal illegality, and necessity of criminal punishment equivalent to those of the illegal business operations under Items (1), (2), and (3) of Article 225 of the Criminal Law.

2. In determining whether a business operation that violates administrative regulations constitutes the crime of illegal business operation, consideration shall be given as to whether the operation severely disrupts market order. Business operations that, although violating administrative regulations, do not yet severely disrupt market order, shall not be deemed to constitute the crime of illegal business operation.

Relevant Legal Provision:

Article 225 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts:

The People's Procuratorate of Linhe District, Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, charged the defendant Wang Lijun with the crime of illegal business operation. The Linhe District People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, found upon trial that, from November 2014 to January 2015, the defendant Wang Lijun, without having obtained a grain purchase permit and without being registered and issued a business license by the administrative authority for industry and commerce, illegally purchased corn without a license or business license from villages near Bainaobao Town in Linhe District. He sold the purchased corn to the Manhui Depot of Hanggin Rear Banner of the Bayannur Grain and Oil Company, with an illegal business volume of RMB 218,288.6 and an illegal profit of RMB 6,000. After the case was discovered, the defendant Wang Lijun voluntarily surrendered the illegal profit of RMB 6,000. On March 27, 2015, the defendant Wang Lijun voluntarily surrendered to the Economic Investigation Brigade of the Linhe District Public Security Bureau in Bayannur City. The court of first instance held that the defendant Wang Lijun, in violation of national laws and administrative regulations and without permission from the competent grain authority or registration and issuance of a business license by the administrative authority for industry and commerce, illegally purchased corn with an illegal business volume of RMB 218,288.6, which was a relatively large amount, and his conduct constituted the crime of illegal business operation. In view of the defendant Wang Lijun's voluntary surrender to the public security authority after the case was discovered, his voluntary surrender of all illegal gains, and his expression of remorse, and since applying a suspended sentence to him would indeed not pose a risk of further harm to society, the court decided to impose a lighter punishment on the defendant Wang Lijun in accordance with law and to apply a suspended sentence. After the judgment was pronounced, Wang Lijun did not appeal, and the procuratorial authority did not protest; the judgment became legally effective.

On December 16, 2016, the Supreme People's Court issued a retrial decision ([2016] Zui Gao Fa Xing Jian No. 6), instructing the Intermediate People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, to retry this case.

During the retrial, the original defendant Wang Lijun and both the prosecution and the defense had no objection to the facts found in the original judgment. The facts found in the retrial were consistent with those found in the original judgment. The People's Procuratorate of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, submitted that although the conduct of the original defendant Wang Lijun was administratively illegal, it did not possess social harmfulness or necessity of criminal punishment equivalent to the illegal business operations specified in Article 225 of the Criminal Law, and thus did not constitute the crime of illegal business operation, recommending a retrial and acquittal in accordance with law. In court, the original defendant Wang Lijun had no objection to the facts and evidence found in the original trial, but argued that his conduct did not constitute the crime of illegal business operation. The defense counsel argued that the original defendant Wang Lijun's conduct of purchasing corn without a license did not have social harmfulness, criminal illegality, or punishability, did not meet the elements of the crime of illegal business operation under the Criminal Law, and also contravened the principle of restraint in criminal law, and requested that the original defendant Wang Lijun be acquitted.

Judgment:

The Linhe District People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, rendered a criminal judgment ([2016] Nei 0802 Xing Chu No. 54) on April 15, 2016, finding the defendant Wang Lijun guilty of the crime of illegal business operation, sentencing him to one year of imprisonment, suspended for two years, and imposing a fine of RMB 20,000; the illegal profit of RMB 6,000 surrendered by the defendant Wang Lijun was to be turned over to the state treasury by the investigative authority. On December 16, 2016, the Supreme People's Court issued a retrial decision ([2016] Zui Gao Fa Xing Jian No. 6), instructing the Intermediate People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, to retry this case. The Intermediate People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, rendered a criminal judgment ([2017] Nei 08 Xing Zai No. 1) on February 14, 2017: 1. Setting aside the criminal judgment ([2016] Nei 0802 Xing Chu No. 54) of the Linhe District People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region; 2. Acquitting the original defendant Wang Lijun.

Reasoning:

The Intermediate People's Court of Bayannur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, held in the retrial that the facts found in the original judgment—that the original defendant Wang Lijun, from November 2014 to January 2015, purchased and sold corn without having obtained a grain purchase permit or a business license for industry and commerce—were clear, and his conduct violated the then-applicable national regulations on grain circulation management. However, it had not yet reached the degree of harm that severely disrupts market order, and did not possess the social harmfulness, criminal illegality, or necessity of criminal punishment equivalent to the crime of illegal business operation under Article 225 of the Criminal Law. Therefore, it did not constitute the crime of illegal business operation. The original judgment's finding that Wang Lijun constituted the crime of illegal business operation involved an error in the application of law. The opinion of the procuratorial authority—that Wang Lijun's conduct of buying and selling corn without a license or business permit did not constitute the crime of illegal business operation—was well-founded. The opinions of the original defendant Wang Lijun and his defense counsel—that Wang Lijun's conduct did not constitute a crime—were also well-founded.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Xin Yongqing, Bai Ling, He Li)

Guiding Case No. 98

Zhang Qingfu and Zhang Diankai v. Zhu Zhenbiao — dispute over right to life

(Released by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 19, 2018)

Keywords: Civil; right to life; righteous act

Ruling Gist:

Where a person, not acting pursuant to a statutory duty, legal obligation, or contractual duty, engages in conduct to prevent an unlawful infringer from escaping for the purpose of protecting the interests of the state or society or the personal or property safety of another, a people's court may deem such conduct as a righteous act.

Relevant Legal Provisions:

Article 6 of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China
Article 70 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Road Traffic Safety

Basic Facts:

Plaintiffs Zhang Qingfu and Zhang Diankai alleged: On January 9, 2017, the defendant Zhu Zhenbiao drove an Audi sedan to pursue Zhang Yonghuan, who was riding a motorcycle. Thereafter, Zhang Yonghuan abandoned the motorcycle and ran, and the defendant Zhu Zhenbiao also got out of the car and continued pursuing him on foot, ultimately causing Zhang Yonghuan to be hit and killed by a train at the 495-meter mark of the 90th kilometer on the Qiancao Line (Luannan section). During the pursuit, Zhu Zhenbiao disseminated and transmitted false information that Zhang Yonghuan had killed someone in a collision; after Zhang Yonghuan verbally indicated an intention to commit suicide and attempted to commit suicide by hitting a vehicle, Zhu Zhenbiao continued the pursuit, exceeding the necessary limit; during the pursuit, Zhu Zhenbiao held a wooden stool and a wooden stick, posing a threat to Zhang Yonghuan's life, and repeatedly cursed Zhang Yonghuan. Zhu Zhenbiao had subjective intent and clear fault in causing Zhang Yonghuan's death and should bear liability for compensation for Zhang Yonghuan's death.

Defendant Zhu Zhenbiao argued: The defendant's conduct in pursuing the traffic accident hit-and-run perpetrator Zhang Yonghuan constituted a righteous act. He had no subjective fault and no objective illegality, and there was no causal relationship between his conduct and Zhang Yonghuan's death. He should not bear tort liability for Zhang Yonghuan's accidental death.

The court found upon trial: At approximately 11:00 a.m. on January 9, 2017, Zhang Yonghuan was driving a two-wheeled motorcycle from south to north and collided from behind with an unlicensed two-wheeled motorcycle driven by Zhang Yulai in the same direction at the gate of the Pengsheng Aquatic Products Store in Qingtuo, Guliu Line. Zhang Yonghuan fell, Zhang Yulai was knocked down and injured, and the motorcycles were damaged. Zhang Yonghuan then got up, drove the motorcycle away from the scene. This accident was determined by the traffic police department of Caofeidian: Zhang Yonghuan bore primary responsibility, and Zhang Yulai bore secondary responsibility.

At the time of the incident, defendant Zhu Zhenbiao was driving past the accident scene, observed the hit-and-run conduct, and immediately began pursuing in his vehicle. During the pursuit, Zhu Zhenbiao repeatedly called the police to public security departments, including the Liuzan Border Police Station and the 110 Command Center of the Caofeidian Public Security Bureau. The content of the calls mainly was: At the northern culvert on Yidao Dang in Liuzan Town, two motorcycles collided, someone was injured, and the other party fled on a motorcycle; the caller was following the fugitive and requested police dispatch. While driving to pursue Zhang Yonghuan, Zhu Zhenbiao occasionally shouted out things like "This person hit someone and is running away!" When Zhang Yonghuan drove the motorcycle into Xiliangge Village, Hugezhuang Town, Luannan County, he abandoned the motorcycle, entered the home of villager Zheng Rushen through the south gate, took a kitchen knife from the hallway of Zheng Rushen's home, and exited through the north gate. Upon seeing Zhang Yonghuan holding the knife, Zhu Zhenbiao picked up a wooden stool from Zheng Rushen's home and continued the pursuit. Zheng Rushen then caught up to Zhu Zhenbiao, retrieved the wooden stool, and Zhu Zhenbiao continued the pursuit holding a wooden stick. During the pursuit, there was exchange: Zhu Zhenbiao shouted, "You killed someone, where are you running? The police are coming soon!"; Zhang Yonghuan said, "In a little while I'll cut myself"; Zhu Zhenbiao said, "If you throw the knife away, I won't chase you."

After leaving Xiliangge Village, Zhang Yonghuan ran onto the Luanhai Highway and made movements to collide with passing vehicles. After being knocked down by a van driven by Li Jiangbo, Zhang Yonghuan immediately stood up, walked a short distance on the road, then turned and ran toward open land in the direction of the railway. During this process, Zheng Zuoliang, deputy captain of the Road Administration Law Enforcement Brigade of the Caofeidian District Transportation Bureau, and others joined in, continuing the pursuit together with Zhu Zhenbiao and warning vehicles on the road to drive slowly and carefully, as this person intended to hit a vehicle.

When Zhang Yonghuan reached the Qiancao Railway, he climbed over the guardrail and walked along the cutting. Zhu Zhenbiao also climbed over the guardrail and continued to follow. Zhu Zhenbiao pursued while advising Zhang Yonghuan: "The person you hit is all right, and you have a family; they will worry about you if they know. Just surrender yourself." At 11:56 a.m. on January 9, 2017, Zhang Yonghuan voluntarily walked between the two rails. Video from the locomotive of Train No. 51618 showed that Zhu Zhenbiao waved his coat to alert the approaching train. At 12:02 p.m. on January 9, 2017, Zhang Yonghuan was hit by Train No. 51618 traveling from north to south and was later confirmed dead upon examination.

During the entire process of Zhu Zhenbiao following Zhang Yonghuan, the two maintained a certain distance and never had physical contact. Zhu Zhenbiao used words to urge Zhang Yonghuan to surrender, as well as words of scolding.

It was further found that after being injured in the traffic accident with Zhang Yonghuan, Zhang Yulai was taken to Caofeidian District Hospital and Tangshan Workers' Hospital on the same day for treatment, then went home to recuperate the same day, and has not yet undergone a medical injury assessment to date. After Zhang Yonghuan's death, there were two first-order statutory heirs: his father Zhang Qingfu and his son Zhang Diankai.

On October 11, 2017, the Luannan Station of the Daqin Railway Co., Ltd. Daliang Depot (as Party A) and plaintiff Zhang Diankai (as Party B) entered into a "Railway Traffic Accident Handling Agreement". The agreement stated: "At 12:02 on January 9, 2017, Train No. 51618, running between the 495-meter mark of the 90th kilometer from Caobei Station to Luannan Station, struck and killed Zhang Yonghuan, who had entered the railway line without authorization, constituting a general Category B accident. The deceased Zhang Yonghuan bears full responsibility for the accident. The railway authority, having no fault, pays RMB 40,000 in compensation to plaintiff Zhang Diankai."

Judgment:

The Luannan County People's Court of Hebei Province rendered a civil judgment ([2017] Ji 0224 Min Chu No. 3480) on February 12, 2018, dismissing the claims of plaintiffs Zhang Qingfu and Zhang Diankai. After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, plaintiffs Zhang Qingfu and Zhang Diankai disagreed and appealed. During the appeal proceedings, appellants Zhang Qingfu and Zhang Diankai withdrew their appeal. The Intermediate People's Court of Tangshan City, Hebei Province, issued a civil ruling ([2018] Ji 02 Min Zhong No. 2730) on February 28, 2018, permitting appellants Zhang Qingfu and Zhang Diankai to withdraw their appeal. The judgment of first instance became legally effective.

Reasoning:

The effective judgment held: The request by Zhang Qingfu and Zhang Diankai to withdraw their appeal during the second instance trial of this case does not violate legal provisions, and the withdrawal is permitted.

The issues in this case are whether the conduct of defendant Zhu Zhenbiao was illegal; whether defendant Zhu Zhenbiao was at fault for Zhang Yonghuan's death; and whether there is a legal causal relationship between defendant Zhu Zhenbiao's conduct and Zhang Yonghuan's death.

First, after the road traffic accident at issue occurred, Zhang Yulai was injured and unconscious on the ground, and Zhang Yonghuan fled on his motorcycle. Defendant Zhu Zhenbiao, as an eyewitness at the scene, promptly called the police, and then pursued Zhang Yonghuan by car and on foot, urging him to surrender. This conduct itself is not illegal. Further, according to Article 70 of the Law on Road Traffic Safety, upon the occurrence of a traffic accident, the vehicle driver shall immediately stop the vehicle, protect the scene, and rescue the injured. Zhang Yonghuan's hit-and-run conduct was illegal. Defendant Zhu Zhenbiao, an ordinary citizen, stepped forward to stop an ongoing illegal act, which constitutes a righteous act and should be supported and encouraged.

Second, viewed from the process of defendant Zhu Zhenbiao's conduct, he had no intent or negligence to infringe upon Zhang Yonghuan's right to life. According to Zhu Zhenbiao's mobile phone video and the locomotive video footage, the two never had physical contact. When Zhang Yonghuan, holding a knife, stated he would commit suicide to prevent others from pursuing him, Zhu Zhenbiao's picking up a wooden stool and a wooden stick was an act of self-protection. When Zhang Yonghuan stated he would hit a car to commit suicide to prevent others from pursuing him, Zhu Zhenbiao and the road administration personnel offered advice and warned oncoming vehicles. Considering the suddenness of the traffic accident and that Zhang Yulai was unconscious on the ground at the time, Zhu Zhenbiao was unable to accurately assess Zhang Yulai's injuries. During the pursuit, the information he sometimes shouted was inaccurate or his language was uncivil, but this does not constitute fault for civil tort liability, nor does it affect the nature of his pursuit conduct. After Zhang Yonghuan climbed over the railway fence and entered the train operation zone to avoid pursuit, defendant Zhu Zhenbiao promptly shouted warnings and waved his coat to alert the train driver, but still could not prevent Zhang Yonghuan's death. Therefore, there is no legal causal relationship between that result and Zhu Zhenbiao's pursuit conduct.

In summary, the claims of plaintiffs Zhang Qingfu and Zhang Diankai in the first instance lack sufficient grounds and are not supported.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Li Xuejing, Liu Qunyong, Xu Wanqi)

Guiding Case No. 99

Ge Changsheng v. Hong Zhenkuai — dispute over right to reputation and right to honor

(Released by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 19, 2018)

Keywords: Civil; right to reputation; right to honor; heroes and martyrs; social public interest

Ruling Gist:

1. Where conduct infringes upon the reputation, honor, etc., of heroes and martyrs, close relatives of the heroes and martyrs who bring a lawsuit to a people's court in accordance with law shall be accepted by the people's court.

2. The deeds and spirit of heroes and martyrs are the common historical memory of the Chinese nation and an important embodiment of the core values of socialism. The reputation, honor, etc., of heroes and martyrs are protected by law. When hearing cases involving infringement of the reputation, honor, etc., of heroes and martyrs, the people's court shall not only protect the relevant individual rights and interests in accordance with law, but also give play to the function of the judiciary in manifesting public values, and safeguard the social public interest.

3. Any organization or individual that, under the pretext of detailed textual research, debate of viewpoints, or the like, defames or disparages the deeds and spirit of heroes and martyrs constitutes acts of distorting, vilifying, blaspheming, or denying the deeds and spirit of heroes and martyrs, and shall bear legal liability in accordance with law.

Relevant Legal Provisions:

Articles 2 and 15 of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts:

Plaintiff Ge Changsheng alleged: The article "Multiple Inaccuracies in the Elementary School Textbook 'Five Heroes of Langya Mountain'" published by Hong Zhenkuai, and the article "Differences in Details of the 'Five Heroes of Langya Mountain'", under the guise of historical detailed research and academic study, denied the heroes using details, attempting to tarnish the heroic image and reputation of the "Five Heroes of Langya Mountain". He requested that Hong Zhenkuai be ordered to cease the infringement, make a public apology, and eliminate the harmful effects.

Defendant Hong Zhenkuai argued: The articles in question were academic articles without defamatory language. The statements of facts had corresponding grounds, were not fabricated or distorted, and did not constitute insult or defamation, nor did they constitute infringement of reputation. He opposed all of Ge Changsheng's claims.

The court found upon trial: On September 25, 1941, the famous Battle of Langya Mountain took place on Langya Mountain in Yi County. In this battle, the basic facts of the heroic resistance of the "Five Heroes of Langya Mountain" and their great spirit of sacrificing themselves for justice won the high recognition and widespread praise of the entire Chinese people. After the founding of the People's Republic of China, the deeds of the five heroes were included in compulsory education textbooks, and the five heroes were regarded by the people as national heroes of the contemporary Chinese nation in resisting foreign invasion.

On September 9, 2013, Hong Zhenkuai, then the executive editor of the magazine "Yan Huang Chun Qiu", published an article on Caijing.com titled "Multiple Inaccuracies in the Elementary School Textbook 'Five Heroes of Langya Mountain'". The article stated: According to a report by Southern Metropolis Daily on August 31, 2013, Guangzhou Yuexiu police on the evening of August 29 arrested a netizen who had "defamed the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain" on Sina Weibo, and imposed an administrative detention of 7 days for fabricating information and spreading rumors. The so-called "defaming the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain" "rumors" had existed before. According to media reports, the netizen had actually disseminated content from a post on Baidu Tieba on December 14, 2011, titled "The Truth About the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain Turns Out to Be Like This!", which said that among the five heroes, "three were killed on the spot, and later their bodies were thrown off the cliff when the battlefield was cleaned up. The other two were captured alive on the spot, but then, for some reason, they escaped from the Japanese." The 11th issue of 2013 of "Yan Huang Chun Qiu" published an article written by Hong Zhenkuai, "Differences in Details of the 'Five Heroes of Langya Mountain'", which was also published on the magazine's website. The article was divided into sections: "Where Did They Jump Off the Cliff", "How Did They Jump Off the Cliff", "Battle Casualties on Both Sides", "Did the 'Five Heroes' Steal a Villager's Radish", etc. The article cast doubt on details of the deeds of the "Five Heroes of Langya Mountain" by citing different sources, contents, and periods of newspaper and journal materials.

Judgment:

On June 27, 2016, the Xicheng District People's Court of Beijing issued Civil Judgment (2015) Xicheng Min Chu Zi No. 27841: 1. The defendant, Hong Zhenkuai, shall immediately cease the acts infringing upon Ge Zhenlin's right to reputation and honor; 2. Within three days after this judgment takes effect, the defendant Hong Zhenkuai shall publicly publish an apology announcement, apologize to the plaintiff Ge Zhangsheng, and eliminate the adverse effects. The announcement shall be published for five consecutive days, and the media and content of the publication shall be subject to the approval of this court. If not performed within the time limit, this court will publish the main contents of the judgment in relevant media, and the expenses shall be borne by the defendant Hong Zhenkuai. After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, Hong Zhenkuai appealed to the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court. On August 15, 2016, the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court issued Civil Judgment (2016) Jing 02 Min Zhong No. 6272: dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The court in its effective judgment found that: The Langyashan battle, which occurred at Langyashan in Yi County on September 25, 1941, is a famous battle proven by a large amount of evidence. In this battle, the basic fact of the "Langyashan Five Heroes" bravely resisting the enemy and the great spirit of sacrificing their lives for righteousness won high recognition and widespread praise from the people across the country, forming the basis for the lofty reputation and honor of the five heroes. The title "Langyashan Five Heroes" has gained widespread public recognition throughout the military and the entire nation. It is not only a commendation by the state and the public for their great sacrifice as outstanding sons and daughters of the Chinese nation in resisting aggression and defending the country, but also the personal reputation and personal honor they deserve. The "Langyashan Five Heroes" are a heroic group that emerged from the great struggle of the Eighth Route Army, led by the Chinese Communist Party, against Japanese imperialist aggression, and are an important event carrier of the nationwide War of Resistance led by the Chinese Communist Party that achieved final victory. The deeds of the "Langyashan Five Heroes," through widespread dissemination, have become one of the spiritual driving forces inspiring countless Chinese sons and daughters to resist aggression and bravely fight the enemy; they have become one of the sources of the military soul of the people's army vowing to defend national interests and ensure national security. In peacetime, the spirit of the "Langyashan Five Heroes" remains a spiritual guide for the Chinese public to cultivate the determination to fear no hardship, fear no difficulty, and strive lifelong for the country and the people. These heroic martyrs and their spirit have gained broad recognition from the entire nation, are part of the collective memory of the Chinese nation, are one of the cores of the Chinese national spirit, and are also an important content of the core socialist values. The collective memory of the nation, the national spirit, and even the core socialist values have already become part of the social public interest, whether viewed from the history of our country or from the current law.

The articles at issue, from beginning to end, did not make a positive evaluation of the basic fact of the heroic deeds and the spirit of sacrificing their lives for righteousness demonstrated by the "Langyashan Five Heroes" in the battle. Instead, they took as their main clues the examination of details such as "where they jumped off the cliff," "how they jumped," "the battle casualties on both sides," and "whether the Five Heroes pulled up the villagers' radishes," citing materials from different periods and statements from relevant parties at different times, entirely disregarding historical changes, the historical backgrounds in which the materials were formed, and the context of the materials. In the absence of sufficient evidence, the articles at issue made specious speculations, doubts, and even evaluations in many places. Therefore, although the articles at issue did not contain obviously insulting language, by emphasizing details irrelevant or not significantly related to the basic facts, they led readers to question the heroic deeds and the spirit of sacrificing their lives for righteousness of the heroic group of the "Langyashan Five Heroes," thereby denying the truthfulness of the basic facts and diminishing their heroic image and spiritual value. Hong Zhenkuai's manner of conduct conforms to the characteristics of harming others' rights to reputation and honor through denigration and vilification.

The articles at issue, through publication in periodicals and dissemination on the internet, had a relatively large impact nationwide. They not only harmed Ge Zhenlin's personal reputation and honor and hurt Ge Zhangsheng's personal feelings, but also, to a certain extent and degree, injured the national and historical sentiments of the public. In our country, because the spiritual value of the "Langyashan Five Heroes" has been internalized as part of the national spirit and social public interest, this also damaged the social public interest. Hong Zhenkuai, as a person with certain research abilities and proficiency in using internet tools, should have recognized that the publication and dissemination of the articles at issue would harm the reputation and honor of the "Langyashan Five Heroes," cause emotional and mental injury to their close relatives, and also damage the social public interest. Under such circumstances, Hong Zhenkuai had the ability to control the potential harmful consequences of the articles but failed to do so, and still published them in their existing state, thus subjectively having clear fault.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Wang Ping, He Jiangheng, Zhao Yinchen)

Guiding Case No. 100

Shandong Denghai Pioneer Seed Co., Ltd. v. Shaanxi Nongfeng Seed Co., Ltd. and Shanxi Dafeng Seed Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of plant variety right

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on December 19, 2018)

Keywords: civil; infringement of plant variety rights; characteristics and traits; DNA fingerprinting identification; DUS test report; distinctness

Ruling Gist

Determining that the characteristics and traits of the allegedly infringing reproductive material are the same as those of the authorized variety is a prerequisite for finding infringement of a plant variety right. When the DNA fingerprinting identification opinion indicates that the two are the same or highly similar, if the alleged infringer submits a DUS test report demonstrating that through field planting, the accused infringing variety has distinctness compared with the authorized variety, it should be determined that no infringement of the plant variety right has been established.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 2 and Article 6 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of New Plant Varieties

Basic Facts

Pioneer International Seed Company is the holder of the plant variety right for "Xianyu 335." It authorized Shandong Denghai Pioneer Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Denghai Company") as a licensee to file civil lawsuits for infringement of this plant variety right. On March 16, 2014, Denghai Company filed a lawsuit with the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province, alleging that in 2013, Shanxi Dafeng Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Dafeng Company") produced and Shaanxi Nongfeng Seed Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Nongfeng Company") sold maize seeds packaged as "Dafeng 30" which infringed the plant variety right of "Xianyu 335." The Beijing Maize Seed Testing Center, on June 9, 2013, tested the submitted allegedly infringing seeds using the NY/T1432-2007 DNA Fingerprinting Identification Method for Maize Varieties, with a 3730XL genetic analyzer and a 384-well PCR instrument. The conclusion was that the tested sample number YA2196 and the control sample number BGG253 "Xianyu 335" had 40 comparison loci and 0 differential loci, and the conclusion was that they were the same or extremely similar.

The "Explanation of the Trial and Approval Situation of the 'Dafeng 30' Maize Variety" issued by the Shanxi Provincial Agricultural Seed Station on April 25, 2014, recorded: As a variety for which Dafeng Company applied for approval in 2011, "Dafeng 30" was not approved in 2011 because the DNA fingerprinting identification conducted by the Maize Research Center of the Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences found no differences at 40 comparison loci between "Dafeng 30" and "Xianyu 335," and the determination was that the two varieties had no significant differences. Dafeng Company raised an objection, and the station entrusted the Plant Variety Testing Center of the Ministry of Agriculture in 2011 to conduct DUS testing (Distinctness, Uniformity, Stability) on "Dafeng 30." The conclusion was that "Dafeng 30" had distinctness, uniformity, and stability, and was a different variety from "Xianyu 335." The "Dafeng 30" maize seed, as a variety approved for promotion, passed the approval of the Shanxi Provincial and Shaanxi Provincial Crop Variety Approval Committees in February 2012.

In the first instance, Dafeng Company submitted the original "Test Report on Agricultural Plant New Varieties" issued by the Plant Variety Testing Center of the Ministry of Agriculture in December 2011. The test site was the test base of the Plant Variety Testing (Yangling) Sub-center of the Ministry of Agriculture. The test standard followed was the "Guidelines for the DUS Testing of New Plant Varieties - Maize." The test material was provided by the Plant Variety Testing Center of the Ministry of Agriculture, and the test period was one growing cycle. The distinctness column of the test report recorded: Name of similar variety: Jian 2011-001B Xianyu 335; Differential trait: 41* Ear: intensity of anthocyanin coloration of glumes of cob; description of applied variety: 8 strong to very strong; description of similar variety: 5 medium. The attached data results table recorded that the test results for Jian 2011-001A (Dafeng 30) and Jian 2011-001B, besides the '41* Ear', also showed differences in '9 Tassel: intensity of anthocyanin coloration of anthers', being '6 medium to strong, 7 strong'; '24.2* Plant: height', being '5 medium, 7 tall'; '27.2* Ear: length', being '5 medium, 3 short'. Conclusion: 'Dafeng 30' has distinctness, uniformity, and stability.

During the trial of the second instance, Dafeng Company submitted a 'DUS Test Report on Agricultural Plant New Varieties' tested and reviewed on April 28, 2014, affixed with the seals of the Plant Variety Testing (Yangling) Sub-center of the Ministry of Agriculture and the Plant Variety Protection Office of the Ministry of Agriculture. The test standard followed in this report was the 'Guidelines for the Testing of Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability of New Plant Varieties - Maize.' The test period covered two growing cycles: 'April-August 2012, April-August 2013', and the similar variety was 'Xianyu 335'. The recorded differential traits were: '11. Tassel: intensity of anthocyanin coloration of anthers, applied variety 7. strong, similar variety 6. medium to strong'; '41. Kernel: shape, applied variety 5. wedge-shaped, similar variety 4. nearly wedge-shaped'; '42. Ear: intensity of anthocyanin coloration of glumes of cob, applied variety 9. very strong, similar variety 6. medium to strong'. The test conclusion was that 'Dafeng 30' has distinctness, uniformity, and stability.

Judgment

On September 29, 2014, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province issued Judgment (2014) Xi Zhong Min Si Chu Zi No. 132, ordering the dismissal of Denghai Company's claims. Denghai Company refused to accept this and appealed. On March 20, 2015, the Shaanxi High People's Court issued Judgment (2015) Shan Min San Zhong Zi No. 1, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. Denghai Company refused to accept this and applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial. On December 11, 2015, the Supreme People's Court issued Ruling (2015) Min Shen Zi No. 2633, dismissing Denghai Company's application for retrial.

Reasoning

The Supreme People's Court, upon review, found that this case mainly involves the following two issues:

I. The issue of determining whether 'Dafeng 30' has distinctness

When conducting variety approval for major crops in our country, it is required that the variety applying for approval must have obvious differences from other varieties that have already been approved or have been accepted by the variety approval committee at the same level. In the variety approval of 'Dafeng 30' in 2011, after DNA fingerprinting identification, it was determined to have no differences from 'Xianyu 335' and was considered the same variety, thus failing to pass the approval for that year. Dafeng Company raised an objection to the conclusion, claiming that the two varieties had obvious differences in traits and were different varieties, and applied for a field planting test. According to the provisions of the 'Measures for the Examination and Approval of Major Crop Varieties', an applicant who disputes the approval conclusion may apply to the original approval committee for a review. If the variety approval committee office deems it necessary, it may arrange a variety test for one growing cycle before the review. The DUS test report submitted by Dafeng Company in the first instance was completed by the Plant Variety Testing Center of the Ministry of Agriculture, entrusted by the Shanxi Provincial Agricultural Seed Station after Dafeng Company raised its objection. This test report was prepared by the Plant Variety Testing Center of the Ministry of Agriculture in accordance with the provisions of the 'Measures for the Examination and Approval of Major Crop Varieties', designating the corresponding DUS testing institution to conduct field planting, organizing test data according to relevant testing guidelines, performing trait descriptions, and compiling the test report. This test report is authentic, lawful, and relevant to the facts to be proven in dispute. The DUS test report at issue recorded that 'Dafeng 30' had obvious and reproducible differences from the similar variety 'Xianyu 335', complying with the provision in NY/T2232-2012 'Guidelines for the Testing of Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability of New Plant Varieties - Maize' that 'when the applied variety has obvious and reproducible differences from the similar variety in at least one trait, the applied variety can be determined to have distinctness.' Therefore, it can be determined based on the DUS test report at issue that 'Dafeng 30' has distinctness.

II. The issue of whether an infringement should be determined based on the DNA fingerprinting identification opinion

DNA fingerprinting identification technology, as an indoor method for genotypic identity identification, is economical, convenient, unaffected by the environment, and has a short testing cycle. It is conducive to promptly protecting the rights of the right holder, and at the same time can improve the efficiency of distinctness evaluation by screening similar varieties. In practice, it is often used to test the authenticity and uniformity of varieties, and fingerprint databases of relevant varieties have been constructed based on molecular marker technology. The core primers (loci) used in DNA fingerprinting identification do not necessarily correspond to the trait characteristics tested in DUS. The approval authority for plant variety rights conducts substantive examination of the distinctness, uniformity, and stability of applied varieties based on field planting DUS testing. In the approval of major crop varieties, variety testing is also conducted on the basis of the breeding report, comparative test reports, etc., and the traits exhibited by the variety in field planting are tested, analyzed, and evaluated. Therefore, as for reproductive material, its characteristics and traits should be determined based on the trait characteristics identified through field planting DUS testing. Therefore, when the DNA identification opinion indicates identity or high similarity, a paired field DUS test comparison can be directly conducted to determine identity through field phenotype. When the alleged infringer claims to overturn the DNA fingerprinting identification opinion with a distinctness conclusion determined by field planting DUS testing, it should submit evidence to prove this. Since the DUS test report at issue submitted by Dafeng Company proved that, through field planting, 'Dafeng 30' had distinctness compared with 'Xianyu 335', according to the rule for determining infringement of plant variety rights that 'the characteristics and traits of the accused infringing object are the same as those of the authorized variety, or the difference in characteristics and traits is not caused by non-genetic variation,' the characteristics and traits of 'Dafeng 30' and 'Xianyu 335' are not the same, and there is no act of 'Dafeng 30' infringing the plant variety right of 'Xianyu 335'. The production by Dafeng Company and the sale by Nongfeng Company of 'Dafeng 30' did not infringe the plant variety right of 'Xianyu 335'. In summary, Denghai Company's application for retrial is dismissed.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Zhou Xiang, Qian Xiaohong, Luo Xia)

Guiding Case No. 101

Luo Yuanchang v. Pengshui Miao and Tujia Autonomous County Local Maritime Safety Administration of Chongqing Municipality — disclosure of government information dispute

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on December 19, 2018)

Keywords: administrative; disclosure of government information; non-existence of information; search obligation

Ruling Gist

In cases concerning disclosure of government information, where the defendant responds to the plaintiff on the ground that the government information does not exist, the people's court shall examine whether the defendant has fulfilled its duty to search and retrieve in a sufficiently reasonable manner. After the plaintiff has submitted preliminary evidence such as relevant clues that the government information was created or kept by the defendant, if the defendant cannot provide contrary evidence and cannot prove that it has fulfilled its duty to search and retrieve in a sufficiently reasonable manner, the people's court shall not support the defendant's assertion that the government information does not exist.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 2 and Article 13 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Disclosure of Government Information

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Luo Yuanchang, is the owner of the ship Xingyun No. 2 and engaged in shipping, sand mining, and other businesses in the Wujiang River basin. On November 17, 2014, due to the need for a property damage compensation dispute case against Chongqing Datang International Pengshui Hydropower Development Co., Ltd., Luo Yuanchang sent by postal express a written application for disclosure of government information to the defendant, the Pengshui Miao and Tujia Autonomous County Local Maritime Safety Administration of Chongqing Municipality (hereinafter the "Pengshui County Local Maritime Safety Administration"). The specific contents of the application were: 1. Disclose the documents on the establishment, main functions, internal structure, and staffing of the Pengshui Miao and Tujia Autonomous County Harbor and Shipping Administration Office (hereinafter the "Pengshui County Harbor and Shipping Administration Office") and the Pengshui County Local Maritime Safety Administration. 2. Disclose the maritime investigation reports and all other accident materials concerning the following accidents: the two safety accidents of Xingyun No. 2 on May 18, 2008, and September 30, 2008, and the safety accidents of ships including Xinyuan 306, Xinyuan 308, Gaogu 6, and Ronghua that occurred from 2008 to 2010.

After the Pengshui County Local Maritime Safety Administration signed for the application on November 19, 2014, it failed to respond to Luo Yuanchang within the statutory time limit. Luo Yuanchang filed an administrative lawsuit with the Pengshui Miao and Tujia Autonomous County People's Court (hereinafter the "Pengshui County People's Court"). On January 23, 2015, the Pengshui County Local Maritime Safety Administration issued Government Information Notification No. (2015) Peng Hai Chu Gao Zi No. 006, stating: First, regarding the applied-for disclosure of the internal structure names of the Pengshui County Harbor and Shipping Administration Office and the Pengshui County Local Maritime Safety Administration, it informed Luo Yuanchang of the methods and channels for obtaining the information; second, regarding the applied-for disclosure of the maritime investigation reports and all other accident materials, upon investigation, the government information did not exist. On March 31, 2015, the Pengshui County People's Court issued Administrative Judgment (2015) Peng Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 00008 in this case, affirming that the Pengshui County Local Maritime Safety Administration's failure to respond within the statutory time limit after receiving Luo Yuanchang's application for disclosure of government information was illegal.

On April 22, 2015, Luo Yuanchang filed an administrative lawsuit on the ground that the Government Information Notification (2015) Peng Hai Chu Gao Zi No. 006 issued by the Pengshui County Local Maritime Safety Administration was not in conformity with the law and was inconsistent with the facts, requesting the revocation of the said Notification and that the Pengshui County Local Maritime Safety Administration disclose to Luo Yuanchang the maritime investigation reports and all other accident materials concerning the Xingyun No. 2 ship.

Further investigation revealed that Luo Yuanchang submitted materials including the "Investigation and Assessment Report on Navigation Obstruction and Interruption of the Wujiang Pengshui Hydropower Station," the "Report of the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department on Vessel Grounding Accidents in Recent Two Years Due to Irregular Water Storage at the Pengshui Wanzu Hydropower Station on the Wujiang River," and the "Letter of the Chongqing Municipal Development and Reform Commission on Commissioning the Investigation and Assessment of Navigation Obstruction and Interruption of the Wujiang Pengshui Hydropower Station (Yu Fa Gai Neng Han [2009] No. 562)" concerning the grounding of the entire Xingyun No. 2 vessel at Gaogu Changtanzi in Pengshui on May 18, 2008, and its sinking at Gaogu Meitangou in Pengshui on September 30, 2008. During the second-instance proceedings of the case, the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department voluntarily revoked its (2015) Peng Hai Chu Gao Zi No. 006 "Government Information Notification," but Luo Yuanchang insisted on continuing the litigation.

Judgment

The Pengshui Miao-Tujia Autonomous County People's Court rendered the administrative judgment (2015) Peng Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 00039 on June 5, 2015, dismissing Luo Yuanchang's claims. Luo Yuanchang appealed against the first-instance judgment. The Fourth Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing rendered the administrative judgment (2015) Yu Si Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 00050 on September 18, 2015, revoking the (2015) Peng Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 00039 administrative judgment and affirming that the administrative act of the Pengshui Miao-Tujia Autonomous County Local Maritime Department in issuing the (2015) Peng Hai Chu Gao Zi No. 006 "Government Information Notification" on January 23, 2015, was illegal.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: Article 13 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Open Government Information stipulates that, in addition to the government information proactively disclosed by administrative organs as provided for in Articles 9, 10, 11, and 12 of these Regulations, citizens, legal persons, or other organizations may also, based on special needs such as their own production, livelihood, or scientific research, apply to departments of the State Council, local people's governments at all levels, and departments of local people's governments at or above the county level for access to relevant government information. As an administrative organ, the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department had the statutory duty to respond to Luo Yuanchang's application for government information disclosure and to provide the government information. According to Article 2 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Open Government Information, which states that "government information as referred to in these Regulations means information that is produced or obtained by an administrative organ in the course of performing its duties and is recorded or stored in a certain form," the documents Luo Yuanchang applied for disclosure regarding the establishment, main functions, internal structure, and staffing of the Pengshui County Port and Shipping Department and the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department were information produced or obtained by the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department in the course of performing its duties and recorded or stored in a certain form, and therefore constituted government information. The Pengshui County Local Maritime Department had already provided Luo Yuanchang with a copy of Peng Shui Bian Fa (2008) No. 11, the "Notice of the Pengshui Miao-Tujia Autonomous County Organization Establishment Committee on Adjusting the Organization and Staffing of the County Port and Shipping Administrative Agencies," which clearly stated the institutional nature, staffing, main functions, internal structure, and other matters of the Pengshui County Port and Shipping Department and the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department. Luo Yuanchang had been informed of this and confirmed it.

With respect to Luo Yuanchang's application for disclosure of all accident-related materials, including the maritime investigation reports on accidents involving the Xingyun No. 2 vessel and other vessels, according to the relevant provisions of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Investigation and Handling of Inland River Traffic Accidents, the investigation and handling of accidents occurring on inland rivers by vessels falls within the functions of the maritime administration authority. Information produced or obtained in the course of such accident investigation and handling and recorded or stored in a certain form constitutes government information. As the maritime administration authority of Pengshui County, the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department had the duty to initiate investigations and handle inland river traffic accidents occurring within the administrative region of Pengshui County. Information produced or obtained in the course of such accident investigation and handling, recorded or stored in a certain form, constitutes government information. Luo Yuanchang submitted relevant clues regarding the grounding of the entire Xingyun No. 2 vessel at Gaogu Changtanzi in Pengshui on May 18, 2008, and its sinking at Gaogu Meitangou in Pengshui on September 30, 2008. However, item 2 of the (2015) Peng Hai Chu Gao Zi No. 006 "Government Information Notification" issued by the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department informed Luo Yuanchang that the applied-for government information did not exist. This was based solely on the self-statement of the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department, without providing corroborating evidence to prove that it had fulfilled its obligations of inquiry, review, and search. Therefore, the (2015) Peng Hai Chu Gao Zi No. 006 "Government Information Notification" issued by the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department was illegal and should be revoked. During the second-instance proceedings, the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department voluntarily revoked its (2015) Peng Hai Chu Gao Zi No. 006 "Government Information Notification," but Luo Yuanchang insisted on continuing the litigation. Pursuant to Article 74, Paragraph 2, Item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court affirmed that the Pengshui County Local Maritime Department's act of issuing the government information notification was illegal.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Zhang Hongmei, Pu Kaiming, Wang Hong)
